Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Transitions numériques, écologiques, industrielles : les grands défis de notre époque sont aussi ceux de l’Institut Henri Fayol.

Ici se mêlent Informatique, Sciences des données, Management, Sciences humaines et sociales, Génie environnemental pour penser les systèmes complexes de demain : territoires, entreprises, filières industrielles. 

📊 Résilience, performance, durabilité… Nous développons et expérimentons en lien étroit avec les acteurs socio-économique pour répondre aux exigences des transitions actuelles.

✨ Une recherche interdisciplinaire à fort impact, où l’humain est toujours au centre. 

Cette thèse de doctorat sera rattachée au département Génie de l'Environnement pour les Organisations (GEO), membre du Laboratoire CNRS UMR 5600 Environnement Ville et Société (EVS). Pour répondre aux enjeux des transitions écologique, énergétique et industrielle, le département GEO accompagne les acteurs des territoires (acteurs publics et privés) vers une meilleure prise en compte des enjeux environnementaux et de résilience territoriale. Il s'attache ainsi à apporter des solutions nouvelles en matière d'analyse, de modélisation et d'évaluation environnementale des systèmes industriels et territoriaux dans un double contexte d'industrie des futurs et de villes et territoires soutenables.

🏠 Contexte

Présentation du sujet

Le changement climatique met en lumière, comme l'a fait auparavant la crise COVID, les vulnérabilités et liens de dépendance généralisée de nos modes de vie envers les infrastructures, les chaînes de valeur, et modes d'organisation économique et technique, éléments souvent déconnectés de l'usager final, de ses besoins et des conditions d'occupation. Pour le secteur du bâtiment, Cimerman (2023) évoque une tendance depuis plusieurs décennies de « simplification cartésienne » de la conception et de l'opération du bâti. Celle-ci se traduit notamment par le développement d'un imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », se traduisant par une superposition d'éléments techniques complexes (chauffage, ventilation, climatisation), susceptibles d'être pilotés au travers d'outils informatiques et d'une gestion centralisée optimisée (Cimerman, 2023).

Face aux enjeux posés par le changement climatique, deux voies opposées d'adaptation du bâti se dessinent. La première, actuellement dominante, consiste à prolonger cet imaginaire de « bâtiment-machine », rationalisable, mesurable et optimisable, et ce notamment au travers du développement du « smart-building ». Cette approche technosolutionniste apporte des réponses clés-en-main (capteurs, outils de pilotage centralisés, etc.) aux gestionnaires et usagers de bâtiments. Néanmoins, elle présente certains défis pour leur maintenance et leur entretien. Nous pouvons citer le recours massif aux nouvelles technologies, coûteuses, complexes, rapidement obsolètes et dont la fabrication repose en grande partie sur des ressources finies. Cela pose de plus les questions centrales des compétences, de la délégation du savoir et des outils associés à des opérateurs experts externes.

En contrepoint à la première voie, une seconde approche, encore marginale, émerge : celle d'un « bâtiment low-tech ». Popularisée ces dernières années en France par Philippe Bihouix (Bihouix, 2014), la low-tech questionne le rapport à la technologie et aux différentes formes de dépendances qu'elle génère (Tanguy et al., 2023). Dans le secteur du bâtiment, l'application de cette démarche renvoie souvent à la dépendance à la ressource (énergie et matière) : repenser les usages, l'origine des matériaux (réemployés, biosourcés) ou encore la simplicité de l'équipement utilisé. Bien que nécessaires, ces travaux s'intéressent pourtant peu à d'autres formes de dépendances associées à la technique, au titre desquelles nous pouvons citer la dépendance aux savoirs et aux formes d'organisation sociale et économique qui conditionnent l'adéquation, la pérennité et l'efficacité des solutions proposées.

Cette thèse offre ainsi une immersion concrète dans les questions d'adaptation du parc bâti au changement climatique par la « lowtech » à l'interface entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales. Les compétences et l'expérience acquises trouveront une résonance particulière dans un secteur en pleine mutation, où la maîtrise des dépendances techniques, économiques et organisationnelles devient un enjeu central pour la soutenabilité des bâtiments et de leur exploitation.

Contexte scientifique

La littérature consacrée à la low-tech s'est structurée ces dernières années autour d'une critique de la fuite en avant technologique et des dépendances qu'elle engendre (Bihouix, 2014 ; Tanguy et al., 2023). Appliquée au bâtiment, cette littérature reste toutefois majoritairement centrée sur la phase de conception et sur la dépendance à la ressource : sobriété énergétique, choix de matériaux biosourcés ou réemployés, réduction du niveau d'équipement technique.

Deux angles morts en découlent. Le premier concerne la phase d'exploitation : la maintenance et l'entretien, qui représentent pourtant l'essentiel de la durée de vie d'un bâtiment et conditionnent la performance réelle des solutions installées, sont peu traités comme objet de recherche à part entière. Le second concerne la nature même des dépendances étudiées. Au-delà de la ressource, la conduite d'une opération de maintenance mobilise des savoirs et savoir-faire, des outils de diagnostic, des pièces détachées, des prestataires et des chaînes d'approvisionnement, ainsi que des cadres contractuels et réglementaires. Ces dépendances d’ordres cognitives, organisationnelles, économiques restent largement implicites et sous développées dans les travaux existants.

La caractérisation de ces dépendances soulève par ailleurs une question d'échelle. Analysée au seul niveau du bâtiment, la maintenance apparaît comme une somme d'opérations techniques ; replacée à l'échelle urbaine, elle révèle des réseaux d'acteurs, des filières, des compétences localement disponibles ou absentes, et des effets de dépendance mutualisés.

Contexte opérationnel

Du côté des acteurs institutionnels et économiques, de nombreux outils accompagnent aujourd'hui la gestion technique du patrimoine bâti. Nous pouvons citer :

  • les outils de gestion de maintenance assistée par ordinateur (GMAO) et les plateformes de gestion technique du bâtiment (GTB) ;

  • les démarches de modélisation des données du bâtiment (BIM d'exploitation, jumeaux numériques) et les labels associés à la connectivité des bâtiments ;

  • les contrats d'exploitation et de maintenance externalisés, et les dispositifs de garantie de performance énergétique ;

  • les démarches et retours d'expérience issus de la mouvance low-tech (chantiers démonstrateurs, guides praticiens, réseaux associatifs).

Ces dispositifs partagent une orientation commune : ils visent à optimiser la conduite de la maintenance, rarement à interroger les dépendances qu'elle installe. Les démarches low-tech, à l'inverse, portent cette interrogation mais restent au stade de l'expérimentation ponctuelle, sans cadre d'évaluation partagé ni capacité de généralisation à l'échelle d'un parc ou d'un territoire.

Il en résulte, en l'état des connaissances aussi bien scientifiques qu'opérationnelles, qu'il n'existe pas de méthode permettant de rendre visibles et de qualifier les dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments, ni d'évaluer dans quelle mesure une approche low-tech permettrait de les réduire.


🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous

Démarche de la thèse

L'objectif principal de cette thèse est de caractériser les apports d'une approche low-tech pour cartographier et maîtriser, sinon réduire, les différentes formes de dépendances associées à la maintenance et à l'entretien des bâtiments.

Les dépendances analysées s'appuieront sur les techniques, pratiques, outils et réseaux en lien avec la maintenance qui seront mis en évidence dans les deux autres thèses du projet PERENNIS. Cette thèse s'inscrit donc en complète continuité de ces deux travaux.

Dans un premier temps, il s'agira de construire un cadre d'analyse des dépendances liées à la maintenance du bâtiment, articulant quatre registres : les ressources (énergie, matière, pièces détachées), les savoirs et savoir-faire, les acteurs et leurs relations contractuelles, et les réseaux techniques et logistiques. Cette phase s'appuiera sur une revue de la littérature scientifique et « grise », sur un benchmark des pratiques et outils de maintenance existants, et sur des entretiens avec les acteurs du secteur (gestionnaires de patrimoine, bailleurs, mainteneurs, bureaux d'études, collectivités).

Dans un deuxième temps, ce cadre sera mobilisé pour caractériser et rendre visibles les schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, sur un ou plusieurs territoires d'étude. Il s'agira notamment d'identifier les sources de données mobilisables pour objectiver ces schémas, de qualifier les points de fragilité et d'apprécier leur variabilité selon les typologies de bâtiments et les configurations d'acteurs.

Dans un troisième temps, des stratégies prospectives low-tech de maintenance et d'entretien seront proposées et instruites. Il s'agira de construire des scénarios contrastés, d'évaluer leur capacité à réduire la vulnérabilité technique, économique et sociale des opérations de maintenance dans un contexte d'adaptation au changement climatique, et d'en discuter la faisabilité et l'acceptabilité avec les parties prenantes concernées.

Verrous scientifiques :

  • Définition et opérationnalisation de la notion de dépendance appliquée à la maintenance du bâti, au-delà de la seule dépendance à la ressource (savoirs, acteurs, organisations, réseaux)

  • Caractérisation et représentation de schémas de dépendance à l'échelle urbaine, à partir de données hétérogènes et partiellement indisponibles

  • Évaluation prospective de stratégies low-tech en l'absence de retours d'expérience consolidés et de métriques établies

  • Articulation interdisciplinaire entre sciences de l'ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales, et capacité à répliquer l'approche tout en visant la « parcimonie » des méthodes et modèles

Objectifs de développement durable rattachés :

ODD 11 – Villes et communautés durables ·

ODD 12 – Consommation et production responsables

ODD 13 – Mesures relatives à la lutte contre les changements climatiques.


🔍 Ce que nous recherchons

Formation : Bac +5 en ingénierie généraliste, sciences de l'environnement, génie civil ou énergétique du bâtiment, géographie/aménagement, ou discipline connexe. Une formation ou une sensibilité aux sciences humaines et sociales (sociologie des techniques, STS, économie de la fonctionnalité) serait un plus.

Compétences requises :

  • Méthodes qualitatives : conduite et analyse d'entretiens semi-directifs, observation de terrain, analyse de corpus documentaires.

  • Analyse systémique et prospective : capacité à représenter un système sociotechnique, à construire et instruire des scénarios.

  • Connaissance du bâtiment : compréhension du fonctionnement technique du bâti et de ses équipements, et des logiques d'exploitation et de maintenance.

  • Traitement de données : aisance avec des données hétérogènes issues de sources variées ; la maîtrise d'outils de traitement (R, Python) ou de SIG (QGIS) serait appréciée.

  • Gestion de projets : aptitude à structurer et mener des phases de projet de manière autonome, en articulation avec deux autres doctorants du projet.

Langue : français courant et anglais opérationnel (capacité à lire des publications techniques et scientifiques en anglais).

Profil recherché : individus responsables, proactifs, et dotés d'un esprit analytique, capables de faire preuve de rigueur scientifique. Personnes dynamiques, motivées par les enjeux environnementaux et par le questionnement critique de la technique. Capacité d'adaptation, goût pour le travail interdisciplinaire et collaboratif avec des acteurs variés.

Head of FDE Learning Programs
jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About the job

Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Mistral is scaling its FDE organization from its first hire to several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers within two years. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work.

You will own:

  • Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement.

  • Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work.

  • Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work.

  • Strategic bootcamps: Empower client-facing teams of FDEs to drive business and strategic discussions and to set up for success large partnership programs with customers

  • Program ownership: Own the roadmap, curriculum, contributor model, regional delivery, tools, measurement, and central team.

  • Scaling: Launch useful programs now, then adapt them for larger cohorts without making the content generic or relying on a small group of experts.

  • Team building: Launch the first programs, build a network of instructors, and hire the team needed to support several hundred FDEs.

  • Cross-functional work: Work with functional managers, Product, Engineering, Science, People, GTM Enablement, DevRel, and regional leaders.

  • Readiness standards: Ensure FDEs in every region meet the same standard, can find current material, learn from recent customer work, and understand expectations at the next career level.

  • Knowledge structuration: Ensure internal resources are up to date and pushed to the right stakeholders with a knowledge management approach.

How We Work in Solutions

  • We care about people and outputs.

  • What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

  • Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

  • Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

  • We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

  • No politics. Low ego, high standards.

  • We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

About you

You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people.

  • You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated.

  • You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training.

  • You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines.

  • You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention.

  • You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through.

  • You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop.

  • You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners.

  • You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones.

Ideally, you have

  • Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees.

  • Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization.

  • Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs.

  • Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities.

  • Built role- and level-based curricula connected to skills frameworks or career progression.

  • Managed a global program with contributors and learners across multiple regions.

  • Worked closely with Product, Engineering, Science, People, and customer-facing teams.

  • Designed practical assessments, readiness standards, or certification where appropriate.

  • Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling.

  • Worked in AI/ML or another technically complex and fast-changing field.

Why this role matters

Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions.

This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

We want you as a talented AIT Test Engineer to help us in our mission by making sure that NYX can be integrated.

You will be successful in this role if you are able to help us:

  • Prepare, execute and manage the internal or external dynamic testing (vibration test, shock tests,...) of several sub-systems (electronic, fittings, weldings...) and internally developed prototypes

  • Prepare, execute and manage the internal or external thermal testing (cycling, TVAC...) of several sub-systems and internally developed prototypes

  • Write documentation prior and post integration and test activities

  • Prepare, execute and manage other testing activities in AIT domain (e.g.: parachute, EMC, mechanisms, Structural Test Model...)

  • You will manage the testing activities from definition of requirements to post-test reviews

  • You will be responsible of writing, reviewing and executing procedures detailing the setups for integration and tests (in Epsilon3, ODOO, Team Center)

  • You will be responsible for the execution of the tests performed in-house with internal equipment (vibration test bench, thermal vacuum chamber, shock test rig, ...)

  • You will be responsible for the execution of the tests performed in external facilities

  • You will be responsible of the procurement (or rental) of instrumentation and its installation on the items to test

  • You will be expected to interact with other AIT engineers and technicians but also with external stakeholders

  • You will be largely involved in the resolutions of anomalies happening during the integration and tests

  • You will manage the reports to be done at the end of the operations/tests

  • You will give your feedback and report on any blockage or problem during the testing and will work to propose improvements and fixes

  • You will be asked to support the qualification plans of new processes within AIT (welding, fittings...)

  • You will be supporting the Purchase of all the equipment (COTS or not) needed to run the testing activities (Tools, generic GSE)

  • You will be working with AIT technicians and MGSE team to define needs of machined parts and/or tools (proposing design, follow up with MGSE team)


Additional Requirements

  • Versatile, in order to support several activities depending on the workload

  • Being able to manage several topics at the same time (preparation of next tests and execution in parallel)

  • Proficient in following safety standards and maintaining quality control during all assembly and test operations.


Qualifications and experience

  • Engineering degree (Master or PhD) in mechanical science, instrumentation/test or equivalent

  • Experience in the AIT of aerospace vehicles

  • Prior experience with Vibration Tables, Thermal Chambers or similar equipment is a plus

  • Mechanical skills with electrical/digital and electromechanical knowledge would be appreciated


Skills and Behaviors

  • Leadership skills

  • Strong organizing and prioritization of tasks

  • Positive and flexible attitude to get the job done

  • Ability to communicate at all levels of the business in English

  • Organized and rigorous

  • Hands-on approach

  • Inventive and problem solver, team spirit

  • Able to document all tasks in written form

  • Demonstrates behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Vision, Mission, Teamwork, Integrity and Excellence

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
The product you will work on

The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. 


Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.


The ideal candidate is

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.


This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.


Your role and responsibilities

You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.


Build the platform

  • Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.

  • Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.

  • Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.

  • Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.

  • Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.

  • Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior

  • .

Run what you build

  • Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.

  • Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.

  • Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.

  • Be part of a compensated on-call rotation


Set the technical direction

  • Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.

  • Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.

  • Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.


What you need to succeed in this role

  • Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.

  • Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.

  • Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.

  • Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.

  • Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.

  • A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.

  • A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.

  • Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.

  • Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.

  • Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.

  • Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.

  • A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.

  • Experience in using AI for engineering.


Nice to haves

  • Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.

  • Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.

  • Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.

  • Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.

  • Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects


We offer you

At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme.

You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching.

About us

Gridcog is a global SaaS start-up of energy nerds on a mission to accelerate investment in the clean energy transition. We build project modelling software that captures the physical and commercial detail of energy projects, front-of-meter and behind the meter, so our users can make intelligent energy decisions. Our clients have modelled over 17k projects in over 40 markets globally.

Germany is one of our most important markets. We've built a strong brand here and work with some of the most active developers, IPPs and energy companies in the country, including MaxSolar, Lintas, Suncatcher, Octopus Energy Generation, TotalEnergies and Shell.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for a Senior Energy Analyst with deep knowledge of the German power market to join our Berlin office. You'll be the second person in the office and a senior voice for Gridcog in Germany.

Your main job is to own our German customer relationships. You'll make sure customers model their projects well, get real value from Gridcog and keep choosing us. You'll use your market knowledge and network to make Gridcog a trusted voice in the market, help win new customers and make sure the product works for the target customer group. 

What you'll do

Customers (the core of the role)

  • Own a portfolio of German customer relationships as their main point of contact and trusted advisor
  • Lead onboarding and guide customers on best practice modelling of solar, BESS and hybrid projects in Germany
  • Handle complex technical and market questions, such as ancillary market participation, grid connection constraints, AgNes, and merchant versus contracted revenues
  • Spot where accounts can grow and work with account management on renewals and expansion
  • Keep our German datasets current, including market prices, network tariffs and project assumptions

Sales and marketing

  • Lead demos and technical conversations with prospects, including senior stakeholders, e.g., partners, investment managers, MDs

  • Speak and present at industry events

Product

  • Bring German market requirements into product development and make sure they are understood and prioritised
  • Feed market changes into product direction and feature development
  • Test new features against real client use cases

What it's like being second in the office

Much of how we operate in Germany is still being built, and you'll often be the one setting it up. There won't always be a playbook. You'll need to make calls with incomplete information, act on them and adjust as you learn. We value moving fast over getting everything perfect, and we'd rather you ship something good and improve it than hold it back.

To be successful in this role you will have

  • 3 to 10 years' experience in the German power sector, with solid knowledge of market dynamics, regulation and commercial models for utility-scale solar and battery storage
  • A track record of owning client relationships and delivering excellent outcomes for them
  • The confidence and credibility to represent Gridcog externally, lead demos and engage senior stakeholders
  • Comfort working in an unstructured environment, making decisions and learning from what doesn't work

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The AI Customer Success function is being built from the ground up, and this role will help define it internationally. As the first Customer Success Manager in this area, you will own the end-to-end post-sale experience for a portfolio of customers that includes some of the world’s most sophisticated cyber threat intelligence teams and investigators, national security agencies, and financial crime teams. Your mandate is not just to manage accounts—you will help establish the playbook, define what success looks like, and drive a product-led growth motion that turns new customers into long-term, expanding partners.

The impact you will have:

  • Build and ship a v1 onboarding playbook within the first 30 days—a practical, working version built from early customer engagements that can be iterated as you learn what drives adoption across international customer segments.

  • Use AI to build production CS workflows that pull from ChurnZero, Salesforce, Gong, and product usage telemetry to auto-generate account health summaries and QBR drafts—compressing hours of reporting preparation into minutes so you can spend your time on the work that actually requires human judgment.

  • Define and track adoption benchmarks across the portfolio—hands-on-keyboard usage, consumption rates, and account-specific success metrics—and surface at-risk accounts before renewal decisions are made.

  • Identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play within 60 days by working backwards from expansion targets, focusing on the one or two use cases most likely to drive consumption across the customer base.

  • Run executive business reviews and QBRs with senior stakeholders at government agencies and financial institutions internationally—building the trust and credibility that turns TRM from a vendor into a mission-critical partner.

  • Partner with ADs on expansion plays, co-own NRR targets, and build the structured path to proving value for every customer with an expiring or at-risk contract.

  • Close the feedback loop between customers and Product—synthesize adoption blockers, feature gaps, and new use-case opportunities into prioritized, actionable input that informs the roadmap.

  • Design the CS infrastructure and tooling stack that scales as the product grows—you are building the foundation the next CSM hire will inherit.

What we're looking for:

  • Background in cyber or cyber threat intelligence, intelligence agencies, financial crime investigations, or regulatory and compliance environments.

  • 5+ years as an onboarding engineer, customer success manager, deployment strategist, or in another post-sale role with proven ownership of NRR, GRR, and expansion metrics—you have the track record, not just the title.

  • Domain credibility in cyber, national security, or financial crime—you can walk into a room of investigators and earn their trust in the first meeting, not the fifth.

  • Demonstrated zero-to-one builder experience—you have built a CS function, onboarding playbook, or PLG motion from scratch and can point to the specific outcomes it drove.

  • Production AI fluency—you have built real, repeatable AI workflows, not just experiments, that synthesize data from multiple sources into outputs that run consistently and deliver measurable results. You can show the workflow, explain the data logic, and articulate where human judgment stays in the loop.

  • A high level of independence—you set your own agenda, operate without needing constant direction, and ship v1 before you have all the answers.

  • Strong executive presence—you can run a QBR with a senior government stakeholder or financial institution executive and command the room through substance, not just polish.

  • Experience supporting international customers, with the ability to navigate regional, cultural, and time-zone differences.

About the Team:

  • This team focuses on TRM’s AI-driven Intel platform, supporting investigators and cyber teams working on complex cases involving cyber threats.

  • This is the first Customer Success hire dedicated to international customers—you will help build the function from the ground up, with high autonomy, direct access to leadership, and meaningful influence on how TRM approaches customer success globally.

  • The broader TRM CS organization operates distributed, not distant—async-first communication through Slack, strong documentation, and intentional synchronous time for key decisions.

  • You will work directly with the Head of Customer Success and Patrick South, CRO, with close day-to-day collaboration with international Sales teams and Product.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • As a globally distributed team, members work across multiple time zones. This role will primarily align its working hours and customer coverage with international markets, with flexibility to collaborate across regions when needed.

  • Our Customer Success team is fully remote, thriving on asynchronous communication and collaboration through Slack channels and detailed documentation. We hold weekly customer syncs, biweekly health syncs, join our associated POD calls, and regularly engage with customers across international markets. As experts in our craft, we focus on providing support, driving value, and building meaningful relationships with our customers as trusted advisors. We are on the front lines of TRM, ensuring our customers get the most out of the product and bringing valuable insights back to the team.

  • The team moves fast and iterates—v1 ships before it is perfect, and feedback is expected to be direct and specific.

On-Call Responsibilities:

  • End-to-End Ownership: While there is no formal hourly rotation, you will be the primary lead for your area and responsible for customer success across international markets. This requires a high degree of agency and a commitment to seeing mission-critical tasks through to resolution, including the flexibility to handle urgent needs outside of standard hours or on weekends when they arise.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 30 days of joining, you ship a working v1 onboarding playbook built from your first 2–3 accounts—not a slide deck, but a live document with measurable adoption benchmarks that the account team is already using to set customer expectations.

  • Within 6 weeks, you share a draft success-metrics framework at 50% complete with the account team and key customers to validate direction—getting real signal on what drives credit consumption before investing further in building out the full playbook.

  • Within 60 days, you identify and scope the highest-impact PLG play by working backwards from expansion targets—presenting a concrete recommendation to leadership on which use case to prioritize and why, grounded in actual account data from international customers.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure you’re considered.

What to Expect From Our Interview Process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while giving you the opportunity to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, AI skills assessment, and Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Explore your experience, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Dive deeper into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: Typically 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Typically 3–5 interviews to go deeper on your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: We’ll speak with former colleagues who can provide perspective on your work and impact.

  • Offer: If it’s a mutual fit, your recruiter will walk you through your offer and answer your questions.

  • Welcome to TRM: Once you sign, we’ll get you ready for your first day and onboarding.

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

Learn more about interviewing at TRM

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate

  • Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more about Interviewing at TRM

 

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. Learn more about building tools for defenders.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

The Field Application Engineer (FAE) is a hands-on, vehicle system-level role. You will work directly on prototype vehicles and lab cars to investigate complex, cross-subsystem issues, capturing the data needed to reproduce and isolate them. You will also provide diagnostic and integration support on-site at partner facilities. The focus is on getting close to the hardware and the buses, producing clear findings that development teams can act on.

jobs.title: UK New Business Director
Platform Engineer (10x Openings)
jobs.description:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About The Role

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for AI workloads. Our platform is Kubernetes-native, spans multiple regions, and delivers virtual machines, storage, and networking through a fully automated infrastructure stack built on custom Kubernetes operators.

We are building out several platform engineering teams that together own the full stack, from managed bare metal and IaaS through to higher-order platform services. Each team owns a different part of that stack: compute, networking, storage, the control plane and API layer, confidential computing, and the customer-facing surface. The area you work in depends on the team you join and your prior expertise, so no single engineer is expected to cover all of it.

Platform Engineers work at the intersection of infrastructure and software development. Across every team, you will translate three key inputs into durable platform capabilities: product roadmap requirements from the product team, operational learnings from the bring-up teams, and security guidance from the security engineering team. The output of this role is production platform code, not configuration, not runbooks.

 

What You Will Be Doing

Common across every platform engineering team:

  • Design and implement Kubernetes operators and controllers that manage the lifecycle of platform resources.

  • Work closely with the product team to turn roadmap requirements into the platform capabilities that support them.

  • Collaborate with the bring-up teams to identify operational pain points and turn them into scalable platform features.

  • Integrate security guidance from the security engineering team into platform-level controls, and remediate findings at the platform layer.

  • Treat observability as a platform concern: instrument services, define meaningful metrics, and build tooling that gives the team visibility into platform health.

  • Own the services you build in production, including participation in an on-call rotation, incident response, and the follow-up work that closes structural gaps rather than only the immediate issue.

  • Hold to clean interface and versioning practice on anything other teams or customers depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes.

  • Participate in code review, technical design discussions, and cross-team collaboration in an Agile (Kanban or Scrum) environment.

Depending on your team and background, you will go deep in some of the following:

  • Control plane and APIs: improve and extend the API layer between user-facing services and the underlying platform, with disciplined versioning and backward compatibility.

  • Compute: build and operate the lifecycle of virtualized and bare metal compute resources.

  • Storage: provisioning workflows, attachment reliability, performance tuning, and failure handling.

  • Confidential computing: build and extend confidential computing capabilities across the stack, from secure bare metal and confidential VMs to Confidential Containers (CoCo).

  • Customer-facing services: the platform surfaces customers interact with directly, including the APIs and interfaces through which they consume capacity, working alongside product and UX.

 

What You Bring

  • 3 to 5 years of software engineering experience, with a meaningful portion spent on infrastructure or platform systems.

  • Strong backend or systems programming experience in a production environment. Our working languages are Python, Go, and Rust; we welcome strong engineers from other compiled or object-oriented languages (for example C++, C#, or Java) who are ready to work across our stack as it evolves.

  • Solid understanding of Kubernetes internals: the control loop model, CRDs, controllers and operators, and reliable reconciliation logic.

  • Comfortable working close to the infrastructure layer: Linux, networking fundamentals, and distributed systems behavior.

  • Experience designing, building, and versioning production-grade APIs or service interfaces that other teams depend on, including disciplined handling of breaking changes and backward compatibility.

  • Experience operating what you build: debugging production systems, and taking part in on-call or incident response.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals: clean code, testing, version control, code review, and CI/CD practices.

Nice to Have (But Not Essential)

None of these are required. Several map to specific teams, so strength in one or more helps us match you to the right one:

  • Fluency with AI-assisted development: agentic CLI tools, IDE assistants, and orchestrating multiple coding agents through MCP, skills, or APIs to amplify delivery.

  • Depth in Go or Rust beyond working proficiency.

  • Familiarity with confidential computing technologies: TEEs, AMD SEV, Intel TDX, or Confidential Containers (CoCo).

  • Experience integrating security requirements into platform or infrastructure systems.

  • Familiarity with high-performance networking: overlay protocols, BGP, RDMA, or packet-processing frameworks.

  • Hands-on experience with distributed storage systems (Ceph or similar) at an engineering level.

  • Background building Kubernetes operators using frameworks such as Kopf, controller-runtime, or similar.

  • Experience with observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or structured logging in distributed systems.

  • Experience building SaaS or PaaS layers on top of an IaaS platform.

  • Exposure to serverless or inference serving infrastructure.

  • Exposure to GPU infrastructure or HPC environments.

  • Experience working distributed across time zones with counterparts in other regions.

    REQ-79

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.
As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

  • Competitive salary based on the work you do here, not your previous salary

  • Equity in Volta, giving you the opportunity to share in the company's long-term success

  • Retirement/pension contributions

  • Comprehensive health, wellbeing and insurance benefits

  • Generous number of vacation days each year

Additional Information

Background Checks

All offers of employment at Volta are conditional on the satisfactory completion of pre-employment screening, which includes confirmation of your right to work, verification of your employment history and a criminal record check, where this is permitted by local law. Screening is carried out by Zinc, an accredited third-party provider, after an offer is made and all information is handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable data protection law.

Equal Opportunity

Volta is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and make employment decisions based on skills, qualifications, experience and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Accessibility

Volta is committed to providing an accessible recruitment experience for all candidates. If you require accommodations or adjustments at any stage of the application or interview process, please contact us at

Candidate Privacy Notice

By applying, you consent to the processing of your personal data for recruitment purposes in accordance with applicable data protection laws, including the UK GDPR, EU GDPR and relevant US state privacy regulations. Your data will be shared only with those involved in the hiring process and will not be used for unrelated purposes. For details, see our Recruitment & Candidate Privacy Notice.

Note to Recruitment Agencies

Volta does not accept unsolicited CVs or candidate profiles from recruitment agencies. Any unsolicited submissions, including those sent directly to hiring managers or employees, will be treated as the property of Volta. No agency fees will be payable unless a valid, signed recruitment agreement is in place, and the agency has been specifically engaged for the relevant vacancy.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative - Spanish Speaking
jobs.description:
About Prelude

Prelude is redefining how companies authenticate and onboard users - turning what's traditionally a cost center into a growth lever.

Our flagship product lets businesses send OTP codes with the best price-to-conversion ratio on the market, dynamically selecting the most effective channel in real time (optimized SMS, WhatsApp, and more) while actively blocking spam and fraud that legacy providers miss.

Founded in 2022 by former Zenly team members who lived the pain of broken SMS authentication firsthand, we're already serving fast-growing companies across Europe and are expanding into the US.

But authentication is only the starting point - we're building the platform for trust at scale, with an ambitious roadmap of market-defining products ahead.

Why join us

Today, we're a team of 60 and growing, based in Paris, building products that power secure and high-performance user onboarding for companies across the world. We believe small, highly skilled teams outperform large, fragmented organizations, and we are intentional about staying focused on impact, quality, and speed.

We operate with a flat org structure and value in-person collaboration, which helps ideas move faster, decisions stay grounded, and teams take full ownership of what they build.
Our values

  • Care
    We care deeply about our customers, our teammates, and the quality and reliability of what we ship.

  • Bias for Action
    We move fast, test in the real world, and iterate quickly rather than over-optimizing in theory.

  • Ownership
    We take responsibility end to end, from identifying problems to delivering outcomes and learning from results.

About the role

As a core member of our Sales team, you’ll connect with a wide range of prospects and spark their interest in our authentication tech. You’ll be on the front lines of our growth engine, partnering with AEs and other BDRs to uncover opportunities, start meaningful conversations, fuel a steady pipeline of qualified leads, and own the full lifecycle for smaller deals.

What you'll do

As a Business Development Representative, you’ll focus on getting companies excited about our product. You’ll be reaching out to prospects across every level - from procurement managers and lead engineers to heads of anti-fraud, platform owners, CTOs, CPOs, and even CEOs. Your day-to-day will involve:

  • Generating new sales opportunities for Prelude

  • Identifying companies and people to target within your verticals/territories

  • Cold calling and emailing as well as experimenting with other channels to find new leads

  • Qualifying leads and pitching Prelude's value proposition

  • Closing smaller deals independently

  • Maintaining a clean CRM

  • Improving processes as we scale our business

About you:

  • You have 6 months to 1 year of BDR or sales experience, ideally selling a technical product at a startup, scale-up, or SaaS company

  • You can handle the friction and challenges of cold calling and outbound prospecting

  • Solid understanding of qualification fundamentals

  • Able to understand technical concepts and translate them into business terms

  • A proactive mindset, with a drive to start conversations, build momentum, and close deals

  • Structured and rigorous in managing your pipeline, CRM hygiene, and performance metrics

  • You know your way around HubSpot, Sales Navigator, Apollo, RingOver, or Kaspr

  • You thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, taking initiative and finding solutions

  • Strong interpersonal skills and an excellent team player

  • Curious, coachable, and eager to learn by doing

  • Fluency in selling a technical product in Spanish

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation package (base + uncapped commission)

  • Comprehensive health insurance plan

  • Urban Sports Club gym membership

  • 100% transport subsidised

  • Swile meal vouchers

  • Pet-friendly office environment

  • Free snacks and drinks in the office

  • Laptop and equipment needed to do the role

  • Hybrid working style: 4 days at the office and 1 day at home, with 4 weeks of remote working per year

  • An annual offsite in a great location (last one was at Le Pradet)

Interview process

  • Call with recruiter

  • Call with a Sales team member

  • Case study

  • A visit to our offices to meet the team and interview with our CEO

We don't expect you to ace all these stages - we will evaluate your creativity and how you approach difficult problems. You should consider applying even if you don't meet all the criteria; we'll carefully review all of the applications we receive.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Success Engineer
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based at our HQ in Munich or Cologne.

About the role

You solve the hard technical problems on live systems.

Once a customer is running on blp, their processes are business critical. Invoices post or they do not. Orders flow or they sit. Our support organisation resolves most of what comes in, and a lot of it is genuinely well handled by people early in their career. What is left is yours: the cases where the cause is not obvious, where it crosses systems, data and process logic at once, where the same symptom has three possible explanations and only one of them is right.

That is the job. Not a queue, and not the easy half of one. Everything difficult that comes out of the run phase lands with you.

Two things sit alongside the case work, and they are what make this a senior job rather than a harder version of a junior one.

Stabilising accounts
When an account's health goes bad, you go in and stabilise it. Not as a permanent assignment, but as a small, highly skilled squad that takes a customer whose numbers or whose confidence have slipped, works out what is actually wrong across the whole picture, fixes it, and hands back a customer who is running properly again. It is the most concentrated version of this work there is.

Taking effort out permanently
Anything that keeps arriving in the queue is a signal, and the answer is usually not more people answering it. It might be better self-service for customers, a customer-facing assistant that resolves the routine questions before they reach us, better diagnostics, or a change in how something is configured at deployment so the problem never occurs. You are expected to find those, make the case, and drive them through. That is how a support organisation scales without scaling headcount one for one, and it is value the customer feels directly.

You work across the boundary between what our platform does, what the customer's ERP does, and what their data actually looks like. You are the one who can read a failing case end to end and say what really happened, and then say credibly whether the fix is configuration, data, process, or a genuine product issue. When it is a product issue, you are the counterpart to our engineering and product teams: you bring the evidence, and because you have seen the same structural problem across several customers, your case is the one that moves the roadmap.

You are also how this function gets better rather than just bigger. The diagnostic tooling, the patterns, the documentation that lets a first-year person resolve what used to take a senior one: that is yours to build. And the interns and specialists coming through the team learn this craft from you.

You do not deliver integrations and you do not run go-lives. Our integrations engineers and technical project managers own that. You own what happens once it is live and it is challenging.

What you'll do

  • Own the technically difficult cases from our live customer base, end to end, to a verified root cause.

  • Diagnose across boundaries: platform behaviour, ERP behaviour, master data and process logic.

  • Decide what the real fix is, and make it: configuration, data, process, or a case for engineering.

  • Go into accounts with a deteriorating health score, diagnose across the whole picture, stabilise them and hand them back running properly.

  • Drive strategic initiatives that permanently reduce effort and improve the customer experience, from better diagnostics to customer-facing self-service and assistants.

  • Act as the counterpart to Product and Engineering, with evidence strong enough to change priorities.

  • Recognise structural problems across customers and push for them to be solved once.

  • Build the diagnostic tooling, patterns and documentation that raise what the rest of the team can resolve alone.

  • Mentor interns and earlier-career colleagues, and raise the technical bar of the function.

  • Support Consultants and Customer Success Managers on the technical substance of customer escalations.

What we're really looking for

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

  • Root Cause, Not Symptom – You are not finished when it stops happening. You are finished when you know why.

  • Cross-Boundary Reasoning – You hold platform, ERP, data and process in your head at once and find where the truth is.

  • Credible Both Ways – You explain the same problem to an engineer and to a CFO, and both of them believe you.

  • Leverage – Your instinct is to remove the next hundred cases, not only to close this one. You would rather build the thing that makes a problem stop arriving.

  • Calm Under Escalation – When a business-critical process is stopped, you get more precise rather than faster.

  • Stabilizer Under Pressure: An unhappy client is not a fire to put out. It is a relationship to rebuild. You bring the temperature down, put structure back into the account, and align next steps so trust returns, not just silence

What you'll bring

  • Master's degree in a STEM field: computer science, engineering, information systems, mathematics, physics or similar. Strong candidates from a related field are welcome to make their case.

  • 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: application support at depth, technical consulting, solution engineering, integration engineering or equivalent.

  • Demonstrable debugging ability across systems, not only within one. APIs, data mapping, interfaces, logs.

  • Comfortable with data. SQL or equivalent, and the instinct to check rather than assume.

  • German and English, both fluent. This is a hard requirement. Our customers work in German every day and our internal work runs in English.

  • Nice to have: ERP experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or similar, scripting in any language, or exposure to workflow automation and process mining.

What you'll get

  • The hard problems, not the queue.

  • Influence on the product, with a direct line to Engineering and Product.

  • Room to shape the function, since the practice is still being built.

  • Real growth – the path from here leads into Consulting, technical leadership within Customer Success, or Product.

  • Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

  • Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

  • Visits & offsites – including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

IFRS-Transformation: Gestalte die Umstellung unseres internationalen Reportings auf IFRS zum 01.01.2027 aktiv mit.

Über uns

Wir verstehen die Halbleiterindustrie als ein Universum voller Möglichkeiten. Wir erkennen Chancen und sehen das transformative Potenzial, das unsere Graphen-Lösungen für die Neugestaltung der Branche mit sich bringen.

Diese Vision ist es, zu zeigen, dass grundlegende Veränderungen möglich sind. Mit Deinem Wissen und Deinen Fähigkeiten kannst Du beweisen, dass Dinge anders – und besser – gemacht werden können.

Gemeinsam haben wir die Kraft, das Paradigma zu verändern, wie die Welt vernetzt ist.

Unsere Technology

Die steigenden Anforderungen der Halbleiterindustrie an leistungsfähigere Chips mit höherer Bandbreite und geringerem Energieverbrauch werden durch unsere Technologie adressiert. Wir ermöglichen die Verbindung von Chips mit Hochdurchsatz-Computernetzwerken bei minimaler Latenz.

Der entscheidende Faktor ist die Nutzung der einzigartigen physikalischen Eigenschaften von Graphen, um elektronische Datenverarbeitung mit photonischer Kommunikation zu vereinen. Dadurch können unzählige Chips miteinander interagieren, als wären sie ein einziges System. Unsere Graphen-Photonik-Innovation hebt Rechenleistung und Effizienz auf ein neues Niveau.

Kurz gesagt: Wir vernetzen Chips zu leistungsstarken, energieeffizienten Systemen und überwinden mit unserer Graphen-Technologie die bisherigen Grenzen der Konnektivität in der Halbleiterindustrie.

Deine Aufgaben

Group Accounting & IFRS: Du baust unsere Group-Accounting- und IFRS-Strukturen weiter auf und entwickelst sie im Zuge unserer internationalen Expansion kontinuierlich weiter.

Konsolidierung & Group Reporting: Du verantwortest zentrale Themen rund um Konsolidierung, Group Reporting und die Weiterentwicklung unserer gruppenweiten Reporting-Strukturen.

Internationale Gesellschaften: Du begleitest den Aufbau und die Integration unserer internationalen Tochtergesellschaften und entwickelst die dafür notwendigen Accounting-Strukturen weiter.

Was wir Dir bieten

Schließ Dich unserem Team an und werde Teil eines Unternehmens, das in der Branche etwas bewirken will.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Since its creation in 2007 in the financial city of Frankfurt am Main, Solactive AG has grown to one of the key players in the indexing space. The German multi-asset index provider focusses on tailor-made indices, offering to its clients a faster service, with greater flexibility and at a reasonable cost. Solactive AG and its subsidiaries have become one of the fastest growing index providers over the past few years and support the leading investment banks and asset managers across the globe. We have gained global recognition for our role in the Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) industry, where we rank among the top providers worldwide for underlying indices. We also excel in diverse areas such as Structured Products and investment mandates, showcasing the wide range of our capabilities. The impact and value we bring to the market is palpable, but also in the reputation we have proudly built by being close to our customers, solidifying Solactive AG as a trusted and reliable ally in the ever-evolving global financial landscape.


Job Overview

Solactive's Aggregate team owns the intraday calculation of our indices: consuming live price streams, applying calculation logic across a wide range of indices, and producing a continuous output stream of index ticks throughout the trading day. The core platform is built in Java and engineered around throughput, latency, and correctness under concurrency, while custom business integrations are built in Python. As a Working Student you join a small team and contribute real, production-bound code to both, working alongside senior engineers who review your work and coach you.


Your Tasks

  • Implement well-scoped features and fixes in the Java calculation platform, such as improvements to calculation components, price stream consumption, or index tick production
  • Write unit, integration, and performance tests, including tests for concurrent code paths where ordering and timing matter
  • Help investigate correctness or performance issues: reproduce them, narrow them down, and propose fixes with senior guidance
  • Build and maintain Python integrations for business teams: connectors to the calculation platform, output adapters, validation checks, and small operational tools
  • Contribute to monitoring and developer tooling that makes calculation behaviour observable and easier to reason about
  • Take part in design and code reviews, ask questions, and document what you learn so the next person can pick it up faster


Your Profile

  • Enrolled student in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field
  • Strong Java fundamentals: object-oriented design, collections, generics, and comfort reading and writing idiomatic modern Java
  • Solid grounding in core computer science: data structures, algorithms, and complexity, and in particular a working understanding of multithreading and concurrency (threads, synchronisation, memory visibility, races and deadlocks)
  • Openness to Python: no prior experience needed, but willingness to pick it up for integration and tooling work alongside Java
  • Familiarity with Git, the command line, and a testing mindset; interest in measuring performance rather than guessing at it
  • Ability to work independently on a scoped task, ask for help early when stuck, and communicate clearly in writing
  • Available for 15–20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks
  • Interest in financial markets, market data, or index calculation is welcome but not required


Our Offer

  • Be part of the Solactive family  an international FinTech environment with flat hierarchies, real ownership, and strong growth opportunities.
  • Enjoy attractive benefits such as team events, Corporate Benefits access, a modern ergonomic office,free beverages and fruit.
  • Work on a real, high-impact production platform and contribute to architectural improvements not just feature tickets.
  • Gain hands-on experience with Java microservices, build systems, and dependency governance while collaborating with experienced engineers.
  • Build practical backend engineering skills that directly support your long-term career development.
